payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and extend storage-system durability. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit corrected the initial claim: the governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, replacing the retracted 12,000-cycle figure. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that temperature, requiring cycling to stop. Sodium-flow architecture separates stack-defined power from tank-defined energy.
